newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - May 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Left-wing Lanka Sama Samaja Party, a member of the ruling People's Alliance, says it is against the sale of 35 percent of Sri Lanka Telecom to the private sector. Telecom is among several government-owned enterprises earmarked for reform.
Farsighted fiscal and monetary policy by government has put the country's economy on the upturn, Deputy Finance Minister G.L. Peiris says.
Journalists demonstrate against the proposed Brodcasting Authority bill tabled in parliament by the government last month. Journlaists say the bill threatens meadia freedom.
A three-day strike by Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor cripples distribution. Talks to end strike unsuccessful.
State sector surveyors begin strike to protest against the government not acting on promises made to them earlier.
Former prime minster Wijeyananda Dahanayake, who died on Sunday at the age of 95, to be buried at a state funeral on Wednesday at his southern home town of Galle.
